analyst_view.overall: A Monday-night Valencian relegation derby: Levante (18th, 11 points) host Elche (19th, 10 points), so the winner climbs past the other and possibly out of the drop zone. Luís Castro has the whole Levante squad available, with Manu Sánchez back from a hamstring injury and only Nakoha listed as a doubt. Martín Anselmi's Elche miss playmaker Marc Aguado (ankle), Adam Boayar and Yago, none of whom the numbers list (they only take off Ali Houary), while Villar, Sangaré and Lemar are back in training, Revivo was a midweek doubt and Cepeda returned late from Chile; Elche have lost their last two without scoring. Referee Francisco José Hernández Maeso (4.2 cards a game) is already counted, but the numbers do not flag the derby or the relegation stakes; no confirmed lineups yet at this refresh, so the view from this morning holds with the card lean trimmed slightly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, high for two bottom-three sides, and their momentum trims Elche only slightly even though they have failed to score in their last two. Elche are without Marc Aguado, who runs their midfield and is not in the numbers, and a six-pointer between sides a point apart tends to be cautious; a mild lean down to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's, and already count Elche's recent 31 corners in six games. Levante should take the initiative at home with Manu Sánchez back on the left, while Elche keep the ball and cross; nothing in the team news shifts that, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already including referee Hernández Maeso (about -12% for his 4.2 a game) and Levante's light recent booking count, which I don't size again. What they don't flag is that this is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between sides a point apart, which usually brings more fouls and bookings; a moderate lean up to about 4.1, a touch below this morning's view because cards takes have run hot lately.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.5 shots and already add for both sides' recent shooting, with Levante conceding 103 in their last six. Levante with Iván Romero and Etta Eyong should press at home, but a nervy six-pointer could slow the game; nothing points clearly either way, so 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Levante have a full squad, and Elche's recent blanks are more about finishing than about getting shots on target, which the numbers' momentum already reflects; without Aguado their supply may dip a little, but not enough to move, so 8.9.
